rows.external_boundary: Standard induced 2-subset permutation action of S4; faithfulness is immediate.

rows.internal_claim: A K4 star cannot be sent to its complementary triangle by the physical S4 carrier action.
rows.external_boundary: J(4,2) has full automorphism group S4 x C2; the extra complement involution is outside the vertex-permutation S4 and exchanges stars with complementary triangles.

rows.internal_claim: q_AB=-1,q_AC=-1,q_AD=+1,q_BC=-1,q_BD=+1,q_CD=+1 arises from the frozen P000/FCC chart sections.

rows.internal_claim: The accepted q is the antibalanced switching class on K4.
rows.external_boundary: Antibalance is classical: switch-equivalent to all-negative, equivalently odd cycles negative and even cycles positive. The checker supplies the project-instance reduction h=(+,+,+,-).

rows.internal_claim: Every q triangle has product -1 and all cycle products are switching/gauge invariant.
rows.external_boundary: Cycle-sign invariance under switching and graph-signature holonomy are standard.

rows.internal_claim: No vertex switching makes q all-positive; equivalently no global signed trivialization exists at carrier-sign level.
rows.external_boundary: Classical balance theorem: switch-to-all-positive iff all cycle signs are positive. Here triangle signs are negative.

rows.internal_claim: The q switching class is a coset modulo the K4 cut/cocycle code; graph H1 cycle coordinates are (1,1,1) for a standard fundamental-cycle basis.
rows.external_boundary: Solé-Zaslavsky identify switching classes with cosets of the cocycle/cut code; the coordinate (1,1,1) is the finite specialization.

rows.internal_claim: The full carrier S4 stabilizes [q].
rows.external_boundary: Cameron supplies the automorphism-of-switching-class framework. The specific stability follows because q switches to the all-negative K4 representative, which S4 fixes strictly.

rows.internal_claim: There exists one representative fixed by all carrier S4; Cameron's first obstruction gamma vanishes.
rows.external_boundary: Cameron's criterion gamma=0 iff the automorphism group fixes a graph/signature in the switching class is exact prior art; gamma=0 here is the task-specific all-negative normal-form computation.

rows.internal_claim: In the original q gauge, g_sigma(i)=h_i h_{sigma^{-1}(i)} supplies the S4 gauge correction and obeys the exact 1-cocycle law.
rows.external_boundary: Cohomological automorphism corrections are classical; the displayed coboundary is the exact finite specialization for this q.

rows.internal_claim: A second group-cohomology class beta controls lift of the switching-class automorphism group to the canonical double cover.
rows.external_boundary: Cameron 1977, as summarized in Zaslavsky's annotated bibliography, states beta=0 iff G can be realized as an automorphism group of the canonical double covering graph.

rows.internal_claim: For this q, the canonical signed double cover is K4,4 minus a perfect matching ~= Q3, and the carrier lift is split S4 x C2; hence beta=0.
rows.external_boundary: Canonical-cover lifting is classical and cube/octahedral symmetry is classical; the explicit identification and split lift for the frozen q are finite project-instance calculations.

rows.internal_claim: For a=(BCD), b=(AB), split lifts satisfy A~^3=B~^2=(A~B~)^4=e, so (alpha,beta,gamma)=(0,0,0).
rows.external_boundary: Group extension/projective-lift machinery is standard; these exact residues are the finite specialization of the split lift.

rows.internal_claim: Binary octahedral / GL(2,3) and other nonsplit C2 central extensions are known comparison objects, but q does not force any of them.
rows.external_boundary: Known order-48 central extensions include A4⋊C4, binary octahedral CSU(2,3), and GL(2,3), each with central C2 and S4 quotient. The carrier computation instead selects the split class.
